drs: Drag Reduction System — a rear-wing flap that opens on straights to reduce drag and aid overtaking.
undercut: Pitting earlier than the car ahead so fresh tyres gain enough time to come out in front after they pit.
overcut: Staying out longer than the car ahead, banking on cleaner air and tyre warm-up to gain the position when they pit.
tyre deg: Tyre degradation — the gradual loss of grip and lap time as a tyre wears.
stint: A continuous run on one set of tyres between pit stops.
pit window: The lap range where pitting is strategically optimal given tyre life and traffic.
dirty air: Turbulent airflow behind another car that reduces downforce and overheats tyres.
slipstream: The low-drag tow created behind another car, used to close a gap on straights.
gap: Time difference between two cars, measured at a fixed point on track.
sector: One of three timed segments that together make up a full lap.
speed: Vehicle speed in km/h, sampled at ~200 points across the lap.
throttle: Throttle application as a percentage (0–100%) over the lap distance.
brake: Brake application as a binary on/off signal over the lap distance.
rpm: Revolutions per minute — engine speed. Higher RPM means the engine is working harder.
gear: Transmission gear engaged (1–8). Helps read corner-exit traction and acceleration phases.
undercut risk: How likely the car behind is to pit early and emerge ahead on fresh tyres. High = rival can leapfrog you.
overcut risk: How likely staying out gains position when rivals pit. High = clean air and tyre life support the overcut.
confidence band: Reliability of this strategy call. High = strong telemetry signal. Low = limited data, treat as estimate.
cliff: The lap where pace drops sharply as tyre rubber degrades past a threshold. After the cliff, lap times fall fast.
safety car: SC — a pace car deployed on track to neutralise the race. Lapped cars may pass before it withdraws.
vsc: Virtual Safety Car — all cars must maintain a prescribed delta time without bunching. No physical pace car on track.
telemetry: Raw sensor data from the car: speed, throttle position, brake pressure, gear, RPM sampled every 10–20 metres.
race: R — the main event. Full race distance, race tyres, pit stops allowed.
qualifying: Q — single-lap elimination format to set the grid order. No pit strategy, only fastest time counts.
fp1: Free Practice 1 — first of three unclassified practice sessions. Teams gather tyre data and setup balance.
fp2: Free Practice 2 — second practice session. Often used for long-run pace and race simulation.
fp3: Free Practice 3 — final session before qualifying. Teams finalise setup and test qualifying modes.
track limits: Art 33 — a driver must keep at least two wheels on the white line defining the track edge. Exceeding it invalidates the lap time.
verdict likelihood: RAG output — whether the cited regulation favours the team, the stewards, or is genuinely contested.
